paras: Induction: gathering attention without disappearing

A hypnotic induction is a set of words and actions that bring you into a state that is receptive to your own words and images. A standard induction is not necessary; in fact, it's an impediment if you're already in a trance state from meditation, loveyhuasca, a lucid dream, dealing with grief, listening to music, prayer, tiredness, or whatever. If that's the case, skip ahead to Orient and contain yourself . But if you're sober and feeling distracted, rational, analytical, or otherwise guarded, an actual induction may be helpful. It doesn't mean surrendering to someone else or playing asleep.
How trancey to be (optional)
What an induction is actually doing

Any set of actions that you take to prepare for a session, to concentrate your attention, or to deepen your state is an induction. It can be as simple as counting or as complex as you might see in the movies. It can also be talking, telling a story, moving around, or just about anything else. The only rule is that if you are using induction, you call it induction.
1. Test with simple target & suggestion (optional)
Please don’t put six metaphors in one trance

Decide what the induction will be for. You can switch metaphors but be conscious when you do. Choose one anchor / imagery and stick with it all the way in and all the way out. Will it be warm, firm, directed, open to anything, witnessing, floating, stairs, garden, inner landscape, dialogue with a child, color, or something else?

You can use whatever imagery you want, or none at all. It can be based on all the different senses: movement, words, space, simple knowing, none, etc. But keep the language to the same "world" that you are working in, or, if you are counting, make it relevant to that world. All the way out, reverse the induction. Borrow some of the qualities of these, if you want, but don't make them your identity.

Decide on one verb (e.g., "float," "go," "enter," etc.), one sensory quality (e.g., "bubbly," "exciting," "calm"), one repeated phrase (e.g., "And whenever you hear this word...), and one transitional phrase (e.g., "And now, let's go deeper"). Read the script out loud; long, elegant sentences turn to soup when you are inducted.
Before you begin

Read through the induction and the Come all the way back sections while awake. Also decide what you will work on, what you will put aside, how much time you have, and what the process will be for. You might do it for love, for play, to be confident, to access creativity, for communion with a spirit, or whatever you want. Be sure to leave time to come out and think about what you experienced.

Make sure that you are in a place where you can be physically safe (don't do this while driving, in the water, with machinery, or with other people who need supervision); if you are not sober or you are in a state of acute confusion, take other steps to make yourself safe. Using the next section, already open? is fine, but don't intensify your state.

Decide what kind of supporting voice you want. Are you going to be warm or firm? Let yourself know in advance that your eyes are going to close and that you might come out and go in again (if you want to). Also review how you will come out at the end. If you are going to use a recording, it's helpful (but not essential) to read through the script in advance. Decide on a word to use if you want to stop ("stop," "stop"), decrease the level ("less," or simply open your eyes), or just have the words stop ("quiet"). You are in control, so if you want to stop, you don't have to get permission from some inner part of you to do it; just stop.

If you are unfamiliar with going in and out, practice it before working on any difficult subject matter. You won't have to supervise yourself all the time, and you will find that your responses come more easily and with less effort. Also remember that if you say no, it will still be no. Lack of silence doesn't give permission for a disembodied voice to start narrating.

Utilization is the art of responding to the responses that the induction gives you. You can do this even before you start the induction and you can learn how to do it better in the language of Appendix B . For now, simply know that you will let each response guide you to the next. Notice what's happening, even if it seems that nothing is happening. If you need to know how to do it, see Let the next response guide you , below, but know the safety and exit instructions first.
Induction (if sober) (3 - 5 minutes)
Sober induction: 3–5 minutes

Read the following slowly into a recorder, read it aloud, or just know the movements of your body and read it silently to yourself. Pick one anchor (sound, body contact, two-hand practice, etc.) and one way to start the induction, and use them both throughout wherever there is an anchor mentioned. Pause between paragraphs, but do not read the directions aloud.
Let your eyes rest where they will.

Bring your attention to your chosen surface and start to notice something of it -- any quality that occurs to you -- and continue to notice it. If your attention wanders to a sound or a thought or some other sense of contact, that's fine; if you want, you can make that your new anchor.
Take some time to do that.
If your attention wanders again, that's fine. Just pick a new anchor.

See if you can find something to notice in your chosen anchor that will hold your attention for a while -- maybe a particular aspect of it, maybe just the act of noticing it, maybe something you are hearing in the background -- and let your attention wander to that.
Give yourself some time to do this.
Bring your chosen phrase to mind and let yourself receive it for a while.

If you want to close your eyes (or open them, or soften them) you can do that. Let yourself continue listening in whatever way you are comfortable. You can continue to have your chosen sound in the background if you like.
If it feels right, start counting down from five to one at a comfortable pace.
5. Bring your attention back to your chosen anchor and notice something of it. 4. Collect yourself and focus on that thing. 3. 2. Let yourself listen for a moment. 1.
Bring your chosen concern to mind, or else just hold yourself open to the possibility of contact.
What do you notice now, if anything?
Give yourself time to respond to that question in whatever way you want -- in words, in feelings, by movements, by images, or however you want.
Give yourself time to notice and respond, if you want to.
Already Open: Containment Protocol (when the state is already there, and you don't want it to get more intense, you just want to aim and stabilize it)
Already open? Contain before you deepen

Trigger: the state is already open, e.g. from loveyhuasca, from meditation, from lucid dreaming, from grief, from music, from prayer, from erotic energy, from exhaustion, from being overwhelmed by beauty, etc.
This state is already open. I don't want to make it more intense. I just want to aim it and stabilize it and make sure it's kind.

Ground yourself: look around the room, describe where you are, what the date is, feel your body, wiggle your toes, press your thumbs firmly into your index fingers, and focus very precisely on the physical sensation of friction between the two.

It's okay for this state to open, but I only want to allow as much of it as I can integrate and work with. My physical body is safe. I will not let myself be overwhelmed. I will remain present as my adult self, and not let my inner child take over and get flooded.
Once you feel yourself oriented, choose ONE of the following:

Show me the next piece of information I need to receive -- whether in the form of a thought, a symbol, a feeling, a question, or an impulse to action -- as long as it's in an amount that I can integrate.
Stay awake when your mind likes to escape
Fighting Sleepiness and Escapism (when you want to stay awake during a hypnosis)
Sit up straight, open your eyes, feel your body, and say: "I'm not going anywhere; I'm going to stay right here."

Look around the room, pick an object, focus on it, and feel your spine: "Is this a daydream with useful guidance, is it an emotional experience I need to process, or is it an escape from something I don't want to feel?"
If the answer is guidance or processing, say "OK, show me what I need to do about that." If it's escapism, say "Bring me back to the present moment and show me what I'm avoiding."

If the problem is that stillness in general makes you sleepy, diffuse, or prone to escapism, then instead of trying to go deeper, try going more alert; keep your eyes open, and make yourself do a small, meaningless movement repeatedly while you focus on growing more clearheaded, then stop making the movement deliberately and see if there's an echo that persists: "Keep your eyes open. Every time you press your thumb against your forefinger, get a little more clearheaded. Do it again. Again. And again. Now stop deliberately pressing your fingers together, and notice whether there's an echo in the first second that you don't do it. Keep working at this level of clearheadedness."
The two-hand induction

Two-Hand Induction For when you need to get in there quick, or to link up inner parts in a direct way. Place one hand on your heart. Place the other hand on your solar plexis. Imagine the hand on your heart is your Nurturer. Imagine the hand on your solar plexis is your vulnerable child part. Take some gentle breaths. "With each breath, I remind myself. Love is above. Child is below. Adult is present." "Love sends love down. Child sends signal up. Love sends more love down. Child sends more signal up."
Sleep induction

Sleep induction Scripting hypnagogia in a way that supports inner work is a little different than scripting sleep induction alone. In inner work, you'll wake up and your adult will need to come back online to write stuff down and take action. But, when it's time for sleep, you don't want the analytical part to come back online. You don't want it to see any revelations or take any action. You just want it to go to sleep.

Optional fractionation: practice coming back

Fractionation (optional) This is a technique that therapists sometimes use without telling their patients that they're using it, to make it harder for patients to "break" the trance, because it conditions them into believing that the only answer to any question is to go "deeper". Here, on the other hand, it's good to know that you're using this technique, so that you can make a choice not to use it when you don't want to. "Now, whenever you feel that you've gone deep enough for the kind of work you want to do tonight, just open your eyes and come back to full awareness, and decide to end the session if you want. Or, if you feel like going deeper, just close or soften your eyes again and allow yourself to go deeper. And, again, if you feel you've gone deep enough, just decide to end the session and come back to full awareness whenever you like."
Deepening, if useful

Deepener (optional) "You can go deeper now, if it will be of use to you, and if it will not be of use to you, just remain as awake as you need to be." Imagine a place where your inner parts can meet. Maybe a room in your heart. A garden or temple. A fire where your Protector can stand nearby. A lake. A chair where your adult can sit nearby. Ask yourself, "Who or what wants to speak first?"
Optional trance depth check

How do you know you're in trance deep enough? (optional) "Just give up responsibility and wait. And if it's of use to you, your wise subconscious mind may allow a finger to twitch, or pulse, or lift up, or to warm up, or tingle, or in some way become noticeable to you, to let you know that you are in trance deep enough to proceed with creating your inner meeting space. But don't force it, or pretend to feel it. Just wait with love for as long as you need to."
Some of these things may happen, or none of them may happen. It doesn't mean they're not real. It just means that they're listening.
A shortcut back into hypnosis

Hypnosis shortcut This is a way to get into hypnosis faster. Practice this only after you have another good induction and return sequence that you know works for you. My dad used a mudra (finger position) to help him relax while driving, by touching two fingers together in the "OK" sign. It helped him relax, but it's not a good idea to do something like that while driving, so don't do that.

Pick a word, phrase, or both a word and a gesture (optional), and practice saying it to yourself when you are already in a good state of hypnosis, and when you are in a receptive listening mode, but not in a peak emotional time, or in child state, or in the middle of a traumatic scene. "From now on, whenever I deliberately use this key at an appropriate time and place, I will slip back into this receptive listening mode. And, when I want, I can change the direction of my session, or end it completely, and come back to full awareness." Come back to full awareness, and at an appropriate time in the future, start up a session again, and practice your shortcut. You don't need to do it a set number of times, or to go a certain depth, or to feel any particular thing. Just practice, and make your original longer induction shorter or longer to help it work for you.

Make sure it's working for you, and only when you want it to. Make sure you can change direction and come out of it, too. It shouldn't activate if you don't want it to, and it shouldn't make you obey anyone, or make you feel like you need to pay attention to things, or make you pay attention to things you overhear. It just speeds up how fast you can get into hypnosis. It doesn't allow you to do things you couldn't do otherwise.

You can always un-train yourself from this, if you want, by not rehearsing it anymore. If you are using it with recordings, take it out, or use an app that will not have active instructions in it. Just go back to using your normal induction. If you are having trouble "un-doing" this shortcut and are feeling disoriented, please seek qualified help. Even if you want to keep it, you should always be able to end a session and not be in an altered state afterward, unless you specifically want to be in an altered state at another time.
